info.title: Conductia Phase 1 API
info.description: Non-normative. A developer aid for the /dev-api explorer, not a contract for integrators: it can lag the route handlers under src/app/api/v1, which are the source of truth. Foundation endpoints for deals, memberships, documents, and audit logging. Protected user APIs require a Supabase AAL2 session. Sign in and complete TOTP verification first.

post.description: One engine, two modes. fast: deterministic rule pack only (as-you-type advisory; not audited). full: deterministic first, then the LLM escalation layer — the send-time gate, audited as one 'screen' row (verdict + sha256 of the text). post.summary: Send an email through the screened platform channel
post.description: Runs the full screen first. Since #192 nothing blocks or holds a send: compliant → provider send (status 'sent', audit 'screen' + 'send'); any risk read (hold or blocked, MNPI included) → 200 with riskIssues back to the sender (the Risk Patcher) — nothing stored or sent until the sender resubmits (edited, with the AI's fix, or sendAsIs=true bound to the token). Every stored message sends and carries its riskBand. The full message is stored in outbound_messages (SEC 17a-4 / FINRA 4511 record).

dealId.description: Deal reference (UUID or deal code, matched case-insensitively). A sandbox slug that matches no deal sends untagged instead of failing. A UUID or PREFIX-YYYY-NNN code that matches no deal, or names a deal the caller cannot see, is answered 404 like a missing deal. Any other ref that names a deal the caller cannot see is treated like a slug that matches no deal.

preApproved.description: Sender sign-off claims for Layer 1 flagged terms (#155/#156). Validated server-side by intersection with the hits the rule pack recomputes — fabricated claims are dropped. Validated sign-offs are recorded in the screen audit and passed to the AI layer.

sendAsIs.description: Send despite reported risk issues (#192, MNPI included — nothing blocks). Honored ONLY together with a matching overrideToken; audited as sentAsIs in the screen and send audits. overrideReputational is the pre-#192 alias, still accepted.

overrideToken.description: The token returned by the riskIssues 200 response: the FIRST screen's read, HMAC-signed by the server and bound to the exact screened fields, the sender, and the deal (opaque; expires after one hour). A valid token replays that screen on the resubmit (no second AI call) and the record cites what the sender saw. Missing, forged, edited-content or expired tokens are not errors: the content is screened afresh and a fresh token returned.

overrideReputational.description: Pre-#192 alias of sendAsIs; still accepted.

clientRequestId.description: Idempotency key, one per logical send and reused on retry. The record-first insert claims it per sender: a repeat with a key whose message was sent answers the original 201 (header Idempotent-Replayed: true) without sending again; a repeat while that send is still pending answers 409. Optional: without it every request is a new send.

replyToken.description: A reply from the Deal email thread (#339): the replyToken GET /discovery/deal-email/thread returned, echoed unread, with dealId (the deal code). The token is signed by the server and bound to the caller and the deal; it carries In-Reply-To (the newest message's Message-ID) and References (the conversation root, then the thread's ids, at most 50), so no header text is taken from the request and this route reads no mailbox data. A token for another caller or deal, an expired one (12 hours) or a forged one answers 400 before anything is written. The token also carries the thread's participants: a reply that adds anyone outside them goes out unthreaded, and the screen and send audit rows record replyRecipientsOutsideThread. Both audit rows record replyToSourceItemId. Gmail and the platform transport write the headers; a Microsoft 365 send carries none yet (#96).

201.description: { message: { id, status: sent|held|blocked, verdict, reasons[], rewrite?, llmChecked, riskBand, recipientBoundary: internal|external|unverified, provider, providerMessageId, to[], subject, createdAt } }

post.summary: Smart lookup for an invitation address
post.description:
Identifies the company behind a work email from verified domains the ACTOR may already see, and proposes a least-privilege seat. Creates nothing and confers nothing. A disclosable colleague in the matched bank company may receive their preferred deal role with reason employee_default. For a selected or disclosed company, companyRolePolicy prevents a Member invitation when no active director exists and identifies whether the actor may bootstrap the first Director.

Disclosure is scoped: warnings about an existing platform user, an existing deal seat or a pending invitation appear only for an actor already entitled to that fact. For anyone else the response is byte-identical to one for an unknown address.

patch.summary: Assign, update or complete a rail step
patch.description: Three moves on one step, in one call: hand it to someone (`assignTo`), save working fields (`work`, shallow-merged over what is stored), or close it (`complete`). Each is gated separately — the MD assigns, the MD or the assignee completes and edits, and external seats go through the company permissions deal_steps:assign / :complete / :update_unassigned. Completing validates the step definition’s required fields, advances the rail cursor to the next pending step when the step was current, and writes the audit rows in one transaction; the MD is notified after it commits. A changed or closed step answers 409. A fourth move, `skip`, closes the step with a logged approver and reason (the rail's flag-off skip; the server-model rail uses POST /deals/{dealId}/rail/steps/{stepId}/skip). The approver must hold an active md, deal_team or legal seat on the deal: the route checks it, and the database checks it again under row locks when it records the skip, so a seat lost in between answers the same 400. The name, role and time of the recorded skip come from the server, never from the request. The rail cursor is not moved by a skip.

post.summary: Connect my mailbox (deal_discovery)
post.description: Runs under the caller's own session (requireApiUserScoped); the RPCs act on auth.uid() only and audit each change. Calls mailbox_consent_grant(): requires a live seat from an accepted own-firm invite on a registered mail domain. Idempotent while a consent is open. The opt-in also creates the caller's mailbox source (kind mailbox, the invite address, owned by the caller, active, on the provider whose registration admitted the address) when none exists. An existing row with no owner and no stored items is taken over, not archived: its owner is set to the caller, because the address is the caller's own, proven by the invitation they accepted, and the guard refuses a source with no owner; its status and provider are left as they are. A row owned by someone else is never touched, and an address that more than one provider could read creates nothing. The RPC result and the discovery.mailbox_consented audit detail carry sourceId, sourceCreated and sourceAdopted; the result also carries reading and readingReason (as MailboxConsentStatus), so a source the guard will still refuse, such as another owner's or a paused one, is reported as not read. This route returns the new MailboxConsentStatus. The only verb of this route behind deal_discovery (404 while it is off). The classification worker also reads nothing while deal_discovery is off. An existing row with no owner that still holds stored items is not adopted but archived (renamed <address>~xyz, paused, ownerless and never read), and the caller gets a fresh active source with no history, on the archived row's provider while a registration of that provider may still read the address and otherwise on the one provider that may (when several could and the old one is none of them, no source is created and the operator picks); the guard's last refusal for the address is forgotten, so the new holder's first refusal is audited; the RPC result and the audit detail then carry archivedSourceId, and discovery.mailbox_source_archived is audited. A firm admin can merge the archived history into the fresh source with POST /discovery/mailbox-sources/unify. Eligibility also requires the caller to be MD or deal team on at least one deal of their tenant, for every provider; otherwise 403 not_eligible, and the status then reports reason and readingReason not_on_a_deal. Each time the opt-in binds a source for the caller (created, taken over, or made fresh after an archive) every active, internal firm admin of the tenant and the CCO seated in the bank's own firm gets one mailbox_connected notification naming the address (a CCO of another bank, or a suspended or external one, gets none), and the archived source too when there was one, so an admin can find the history to merge; an archive that leaves no fresh source notifies as well. A repeat call or a re-consent over the caller's own source sends none. Taking over an ownerless source with no stored items also clears its checkpoint and sync state, so the new holder backfills afresh.

StepId.name: stepId
StepId.description: Rail step slug as stored on deal_steps.step_id — `p{phase}-s{seq}`, e.g. p1-s9 (MD Briefing) or p2-s36 (Teaser). Never a UUID.

IgnatiousStepId.name: stepId
IgnatiousStepId.description: Rail step slug. Only p1-s9 (MD Briefing) has an Ignatious skill wired; every other step 404s before the deal is even looked up.

ExecutionId.name: executionId
ExecutionId.description: Run handle returned by the trigger call. Opaque control-plane string, not a UUID.

ArtifactIndex.name: artifact
ArtifactIndex.description: Zero-based index of the artifact in the run's artifact list (run status `artifacts`). The path is resolved server-side; a `path` parameter is refused with 400 so no file name rides in the URL.

can_invite.description: Temporary synchronized projection of the direct company:invites:send grant. It is not an authorization source.
Temporary direct-grant projection. Clients must use company_permissions or member access.

company_permissions.description: Source-aware effective permissions for the user's current company. Empty when company_access_management is off or the user has no company.

PendingQuestion.description: A question the agent is blocked on. Answer it through the run input endpoint.

path.description: Pass to the artifacts endpoint to download the bytes.

RunAccepted.description: A run the control plane has queued. Poll the run endpoint with executionId for progress.

links.description: Control-plane URLs. Informational only — the browser reaches runs through this API, never the control plane directly.

RunStatus.description: A run snapshot. There is no push channel on this API: poll while status is queued or running (the app polls every 2.5s).

filings.description: What the run filed into the deal or lead record.

answers.description: Answers to pendingQuestions. Rows missing questionId or answer are dropped silently rather than failing the batch.

timedOut.description: The operator let the question window lapse; the agent proceeds on its defaults.

BenchSkill.description: One skill on the Ignatious bench, with its routing and load state.

reason.description: Why the skill will not load, when status is not_loadable.

conversationId.description: Continues an existing bench thread. Omit to start one.

selection.description: Which bench stage (and optionally application) the message is aimed at.

model.description: Overrides the bench default. An unrecognised value is ignored, not rejected.

AccessDestination.description: The gated surface the requester wants to reach; each maps to one company permission.

requesterName.description: Resolved for the approver inbox; null on the requester’s own rows.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata only — bytes are never stored.

work.description: The step’s working payload. Stripped to {} for external callers who cannot edit it.

updatedAt.description: The row version. Send it back as expectedUpdatedAt to save against what you read.

sender.description: The sender's display name, else the address. Null unless own.

own.description: The caller's own mailbox holds the message (RLS returned a source_item_texts row; only its id is selected).

opensThread.description: The caller's own connected mailbox holds the message, so GET /discovery/deal-email/thread opens it. False for a colleague's message and for a team inbox item the caller reads as a member: those are listed but do not open.

conversationId.description: The References root (rfc822:<message-id>), or null when the message stands alone.

replyToken.description: The signed threading of a reply to the newest message, with the thread's participants, for POST /outbox; null when that message has no usable Message-ID (the reply then goes out unthreaded). A reply that adds anyone outside the participants goes out unthreaded too.

body.description: The top of the message, quoted history dropped (source_item_texts.body_text).

internetMessageId.description: The RFC 5322 Message-ID, for a reply's In-Reply-To and References.

fromSelf.description: The sender is the caller (their sign-in address): a reply goes to this message's recipients.

eligible.description: A grant would be accepted now: the caller holds a live seat from an accepted own-firm invite, on a registered mail domain, and is MD or deal team on at least one deal of their tenant. The deal test applies when a consent is opened only, so a consented member who has since left every deal reads false here while reading is unaffected.

reason.description: Why not eligible: no_invite (no seat), domain (the address is off the registered mail domains) or not_on_a_deal (the caller is not MD or deal team on any deal of their tenant).

consented.description: The caller holds an open consent on their CURRENT seated invite, the one the guard reads. A consent on an older invite (before a re-invite) never reads anything and is not reported here.

reading.description: Database eligibility: true exactly when the guard allows the caller's seated mailbox address, because the status and the guard ask one decision (mailbox_guard_verdict). The caller holds an open consent on the seated invite, and a source exists for the seated address, is owned by the caller and is active. It does not say a pass has run or will run: the worker's provider group mirror and flags are not database facts. Consent alone is not reading. The card says "You're connected. Conductia reads your mailbox when your firm's reader runs." only when this is true.

readingReason.description: Why reading is false, or null when it is true: the guard's own reason, in the guard's order. no_source: no mailbox source for the address (tested before consent). no_consent: no open consent on the seated invite. owner_mismatch: the source has no owner or belongs to someone else. source_paused: the source is not active. registration_inactive, external, seat_inactive: the source is on a provider whose registration is not active, does not name the caller's company as the firm, or whose seat is not live. Three reasons describe the member and not the address, and stay outside the guard's verdict. no_invite: no seat, whatever the guard's cause. domain: seated, but no provider's registration lists the address's domain for the firm. not_on_a_deal: no open consent, and the caller is not MD or deal team on any deal of their tenant, so connecting is refused; reported only before consent, because the deal test is a grant-time precondition and a consented member who leaves every deal is still read.

staleConsent.description: The caller holds an open consent but none on the current seated invite (an older invite, or no seat at all). Always false when consented is true. It lets the card offer "Stop reading" while it offers Connect.

since.description: When the current consent was granted; null unless consented.

stale.description: The registrant no longer stands as an active, internal admin seated in the registered firm (suspended, removed, made external or stripped of the admin role). The site is not read while this is true; a firm admin who registers it again replaces the row.

TeamMailboxRegistration.description: A team inbox registration (#581) as connect returns it: the address, the Google Directory check and the one source it owns. No mail.

checkStatus.description: pending until the worker's first Directory check; verified once the address is a real, active user mailbox; refused when it is not. A refused check is retried every tick.

checkReason.description: Why a refused check refused; null unless checkStatus is refused.

sourceId.description: The one content source the registration owns.

backfillSince.description: The day the source's first read starts from.

TeamMailboxPerson.description: A colleague a firm admin can let read a team inbox: an active, internal person seated in the inbox's firm who is not a firm admin.

name.description: The display name, else the full name.

TeamMailboxMember.description: A person the firm admin has let read a team inbox.

TeamMailbox.description: One open team inbox registration as discovery_team_mailboxes() lists it: TeamMailboxRegistration plus the state the admin card shows.

lastCheckError.description: A transient failure of the latest check. It never changes checkStatus: a Ready inbox stays Ready.

sourceStatus.description: paused when a firm admin paused the source.

removable.description: True while its source holds no mail, verified or not; only then does DELETE succeed.

readRefusal.description: Why the worker's last read of the inbox was refused (a fixed refusal code), or null once a read is allowed. not_in_provider_group: the address is not a direct member of the ingest group, so a Ready inbox is never read.

members.description: The open members, oldest first. A member promoted to firm admin since stays listed until an admin removes them, though they read nothing.

eligible.description: Everyone who could be a member of this inbox, members included: the active, internal colleagues seated in the inbox's firm who are not firm admins, by name. The card offers eligible minus members.

TeamMailboxAuditInbox.description: One of the caller's firm company's team inboxes, open or closed, oldest first.

address.description: From the registry, lower-cased; null for a closed registration (shown as "Removed inbox").

TeamMailboxAuditDetail.description: The only detail keys the RPC returns, each only when present and well formed; every other key of the audit row is dropped (the pass's registration, worker, jobId, runId and passId, an AI pass's lastRenewedAt, a capability switch's decisionRef, the drift lists, any address or free text).

teamMailboxId.description: Only an inbox of the caller's firm company.

sourceId.description: Only a content source of those inboxes.

change.description: A fixed code matching ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$ (paused, resumed, restarted, window_set).

thisInbox.description: A Google group drift row: one of the caller's own inboxes is missing from the group, or extra in it, or both (one missing and another extra).

path.description: An AI proposal pass's path, a fixed code matching ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$ (recorded, synthetic, verified).

outcome.description: How a finished AI proposal pass ended, a fixed code matching ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$ (complete, page_limit, paused, refused, revoked, archived, error, zdr_unavailable, ledger, failure_streak, unclosed).

asked.description: A finished AI proposal pass: messages asked.

deal.description: A finished AI proposal pass: answers that named a deal.

notDeal.description: A finished AI proposal pass: answers that found no deal.

invalid.description: A finished AI proposal pass: answers that could not be read.

failed.description: A finished AI proposal pass: calls that failed.

items.description: A rule detector pass over the inbox (G-07): the messages the run examined. The pass's run id is never returned.

events.description: A rule detector pass over the inbox (G-07): the milestones the run found.

capability.description: An owner's capability switch for the caller's firm company, a fixed code matching ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$ (team_proposals, milestone_rules, firm_name_alias).

on.description: Whether that capability is now on. The switch's decision reference is never returned.

actorName.description: The acting user's display or full name; null for a service row, or for a name that would carry an '@'.

serviceIdentity.description: A service row's identity when it matches ^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$ (discovery-worker, team-mailbox), else null.

subjectName.description: The person a member_added or member_removed row is about.

inboxId.description: The inbox the row is about; null for a firm event (Google ingest-group drift, or an owner's capability switch for the firm company).

next.description: The keyset of the next, older page (the oldest row of this one), or null on the last page. Pass it back as before=<ts>,<id>.

moved.description: Stored items newly attached to the target.

alreadyLinked.description: Stored items the target already held, so not duplicated.

candidatesRefreshed.description: Candidates whose visibility was rebuilt for the target's owner.

GoogleMailboxStatus.description: What the /profile card needs for a Gmail member after the one-click opt-in (discovery_google_mailbox_status). { connected: false } when the caller has no live Google source of their own.

group.description: The firm's bank-owned ingest group (google_reader_registrations.allowlist_group): the member must be in it.

domain.description: The Workspace domain of the Google registration.

paused.description: A firm admin paused the source.

waitingForGroup.description: The guard's last provider_read refusal for the address was not_in_provider_group (mailbox_guard_state). Clears with the first pass that reads.

state.description: The caller's own source's sync state, by discovery_source_health_state, the precedence discovery_ingestion_health uses (#341). Null when an older database omits it.

backfillCompletedAt.description: When the first full read of the mailbox finished (content_sources.backfill_completed_at).

delegationRefused.description: Google refused the firm's domain-wide delegation for this source: the state is delegation_broken, or the active source's last error is the worker's delegation refusal, written at or after the latest pass started.
